name: Afghanistan
summary: A white field bearing the Shahada, the Islamic declaration of faith, in black. It is the flag of the Taliban's Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, in control since August 2021. The black-red-green tricolour of the former Islamic Republic is still used by many Afghans abroad and at some international bodies.
origin: Afghanistan has changed its flag more often than almost any other country, with over twenty designs since the early 20th century. Black, red and green, with the national emblem of a mosque, featured on most flags from 1928.

The Taliban first used a plain white flag after taking Kabul in 1996, adding the Shahada in 1997. After their removal in 2001 the Islamic Republic used a black-red-green tricolour with the national emblem. When the Taliban retook Kabul on 15 August 2021, they restored the white flag with the Shahada.
The Islamic Emirate is not widely recognised internationally, and the tricolour remains in use at the United Nations and at many Afghan embassies and diaspora events.

symbols.name: Shahada

facts: Afghanistan's flag has changed more often in the 20th century than that of almost any other country.
Saudi Arabia's flag also bears the Shahada, in white on green.
The black-red-green tricolour is still flown by many Afghans as a symbol of the former republic.
